 MR SMIT P VAGHELA(10653) for the Applicant(s) No. 1  MR VAIBHAV A VYAS(2896) for the Applicant(s) No. 1  MR.HITENDRA D RAJPUT(7224) for the Respondent(s) No. 2  MR. CHINTAN DAVE, APP for the Respondent(s) No. 1  ==========================================================

sentences.text:
By way of the present application under Section 438 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973, the Applicant has prayed for enlarging the Applicant on anticipatory bail in connection with the F I R be i ng C. R. No . 1 1 2 0 6 0 4 4 2 4 0 3 1 0 o f 2 0 2 4 registered wit h 'A' Division Police Station,
Mahesana for the offe nce s puni sha bl e unde r S ec tions 406, 420 and 114 of the Indian Penal Code.

2. Heard learned Advocate Mr. Vaibhav A. Vyas for the Applicant, learned APP Mr. Chintan Dave for the Respondent - State and learned Advocate Mr. Hitendra D. Rajput for Respondent No.2.
3.
Learned Advocate Mr. Vaibhav A. Vyas appearing for the Applicant has submitted that the Applicant has not committed any offence as alleged in the FIR.

The Applicant is a partner of the Jignesh Mohanlal Parmar vs State Of Gujarat on 11 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/158555323/
1 partnership firm which was in the business of building houses in the name and style of Himadri Residency.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The firm of which the present Applicant was a partner had NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/12046/2024 ORDER DATED: 11/12/2024 undefined undertaken the task of developing a scheme in the name and style of Himadri Residency.
Accordingly, the firm had undertaken the work of construction and had constructed several houses.
The same had been allotted and sold to the first informant and other victims and the possession of the same has also been handed over.

However,
through inadvertence in the sale deeds which were executed in favour of the first informant as well as the other witnesses the fact as regards the loan of Rs.4 Crore having been procured from Mass Finance Services over the land on which the said residency was developed, could not be mentioned.
The first informant and other allottees were very well aware about the loan having been procured over the land in question.
Therefore, it cannot be said that they were kept in dark by the present Applicant.

He further submitted that out of the loan amount of Rs.4 Crore, the partnership firm had already deposited the amount of Rs.3 Crore and remaining amount of Rs. 1 Crore shall be deposited within reasonable time.

Learned Advocate for the Applicant has submitted that the Applicant is apprehending arrest in connection the aforesaid FIR and in this connection the earlier application filed by the Applicant before the learned Sessions Court came to be dis-allowed.
He submitted that considering the facts stated in the Application, the applicant may be granted anticipatory bail.

4. Learned Additional Public Prosecutor appearing on behalf of the respondent - State has opposed grant of anticipatory bail contending that the present Applicant had willfully concealed the fact as regards loan having been obtained from Mass Financial Services over the land in question.
The first informant and other intimates came to know about the said fact only when they received the notices from Mass Financial Services for repayment of the said loan.
Learned APP has therefore prayed that the present Application may be dismissed.
5. Learned Advocate Mr. Hitendra D. Rajput appearing for the NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/12046/2024 ORDER DATED: 11/12/2024 undefined

Original Complainant has also opposed the Application contending that the loan amount outstanding as on today comes to Rs.11,13,81,842/- against which the Applicant has paid the amount of Rs.3,00,12,543/-.
The remaining amount of Rs.9,70,42,248/- is yet to be recovered from the partnership firm.

He submitted that the Applicant and the other co-accused had kept the first informant and other victims in dark as regards the said loan with a malafide intention and they only came to know about the same when notices were received by them from the said Mass Financial Services.
He therefore prayed to dismiss the present Application.
6. Heard learned Advocates for the parties and perused the record.
The present Applicant happens to be a partner of Himadri Residency.
A Residential Scheme in the said name and style had been proposed by the present Applicant and the other co-accused and the said scheme was to come up on the land mentioned in the FIR.

After the construction of the said scheme was completed, various flats and shops constructed on the land were sold to the first informant as well as other intimates and while executing the sale deeds in their favour it was mentioned in the said sale deed that there was no charge over the property which was transferred in their favour vide respective sale deeds.
Subsequently, the first informant and other allottees received notices from Mass Financial Services asking them to repay the amount of loan which was procured over the property in question.

It was at Jignesh Mohanlal Parmar vs State Of Gujarat on 11 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/158555323/
2

entities.text: Jignesh Mohanlal Parmar vs State Of Gujarat on 11 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: that point of time it came to notice that the present Applicant and the other co-accused had obtained loan worth four crores over the said scheme.

The fact that this aspect had been concealed by the present Applicant and the other co-accused from the first informant and other allottees of the scheme indicates a mala fide intention on their part.

The fact of loan having been procured over the property in question ought not to have been withheld by the present Applicant and the other co-accused from the persons in whose favour sale deeds were executed.

Merely because the possession of the flats / shops had NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/12046/2024 ORDER DATED:
11/12/2024 undefined been handed over by the present Applicant to the respective allottees would not absolve and the other co-accused from criminal liability.
7. Having regard to the aforesaid facts, no case is made out.
The Application is dismissed.

(M. R. MENGDEY,J) J.N.W / 44 Jignesh Mohanlal Parmar vs State Of Gujarat on 11 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/158555323/
